primary_sources.finding: Axiom reports are logInfo messages, not direct flushed file writes.
CLI message reporting is incremental, but uses IO.print or IO.println without an explicit flush here.
Each command runs with isolated standard streams; captured output is converted to a message after command completion.
The isolated in-memory stream implements flush as a no-op.
withIsolatedStreams swaps Lean standard streams for in-memory buffers.
Profiler measurements emit through tout only when the timed scope finishes.
The profiling callback runs in the timer destructor, subject to its threshold.
tout sends profiler text to Lean's stderr stream.
Cumulative profiling output is requested after runFrontend returns.
A separately opened Handle.flush explicitly writes the handle's pending output.
CommandElabM provides the ordinary IO lift used by the diagnostic command.
The diagnostic string argument uses the existing StrLit.getString API.
Axiom collection first consults imported precomputed data; it must not be assumed to traverse all imported proof bodies anew.
Legacy source chooses private global import level; module source chooses exported level.
Module-system roots reject direct legacy imports; legacy roots ignore transitive module visibility boundaries.
The legacy global private level forces transitive importAll.
The documented private import level loads all data; importModules is timed as one import profiler scope.

diagnostic_design.transport: RG_PHASE_LOG names a separate append-only file opened with IO.FS.Handle.mk; every marker explicitly flushes that real file handle.
diagnostic_design.kernel_checkpoint: rg_phase_checked forces env.checked.get.find? on the fully qualified original declaration before recording completion.
diagnostic_design.source_strategy: Separate diagnostic module with exact original imports, declarations, proofs, options and axiom reports, plus one helper import and 26 marker commands. Removing only that instrumentation reconstructs the original bytes exactly.
diagnostic_design.control_strategy: Compile the tiny marker helper and run RGDiagnosticMarkerControl before any expensive RG restore; require all three control markers and normal compiler success.
diagnostic_design.host_strategy: Write and flush a separate process-start record before launching the diagnostic Lean process, then a process-exit or timeout record from the supervising process; retain the separate marker file even on failure.
diagnostic_design.scope: No production Lean source, workflow, manifest or helper is changed. No diagnostic output may enter a production success receipt.
diagnostic_design.limits: Retain one worker, 900-second module timeout, 2048-MiB resource reserve, trust level and all existing compiler proof-checking flags.

interpretation.last_boundary: Process-start only; no header.complete after a successful small marker control
interpretation.conclusion: The diagnostic has not reached the first original declaration. This localizes the delay to startup/import/header/first-command entry, not all_checked/adjacent_checked/budget_checked; do not overstate this as identifying one individual import.
The original X declaration or its kernel completion is the pending stage.
The #print axioms command for X is the pending stage.

interpretation.conclusion: All source commands and named axiom reports completed; investigate post-elaboration/export work separately.

reorganization_constraints: A one-line switch to module is rejected by Lean because BothLong directly imports legacy SliceComplete modules.
Adding ordinary proof chunk files with the same transitive legacy closure cannot remove the existing import byte volume.

A genuine module-system migration must cover the required legacy import boundary and preserve all public statements, original cases, sources, checked proof exports and complete sidecar provenance; it is not proposed blindly here.
